doc.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010

title: Back in Utica: playing with local musicians
summary: LaLama recalls playing in Utica with J.R. Monterose, Nick Brignola and others, and a young Rick Montalbano Jr. sitting in; Rowe notes Utica as a midway point.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Thank you, Monk. Yeah, it’s nice to be here. We had a good gig yesterday, two gigs, yes. People are nice around here. You know I used to play here. Tiny’s and do some concerts, and did a bunch of stuff for J.R. [Monterose], did a couple of benefits for Phyllis [Monterose], I remember with Nick [Brignola] and Joe Mags [Magnarelli] and you know Rick [Montalbano]. I remember Rick [Montalbano] Junior —
Yeah but I mean when he was tiny, man, like he would sit in with us. And yesterday he played the gigs with us.
It sort of makes you feel like am I that old?
I was told Utica, I’m not a native of here but I’m from Rochester, but I was told that Utica used to be like a midway point, sort of guys would travel the Thruway and —
